headline_marked: [[Xbox Game Pass]] cloud gaming now capped at 15 hours/month for Ultimate
headline: Xbox Game Pass cloud gaming now capped at 15 hours/month for Ultimate
summary: Microsoft introduces monthly playtime limits for Xbox Cloud Gaming, forcing subscribers to buy more hours after reaching caps.
details: Microsoft has implemented new monthly playtime limits for its Xbox Cloud Gaming service, a feature of Xbox Game Pass. Starting in November, subscribers across all tiers will face caps on how many hours they can stream games each month. Exceeding these limits will require players to purchase additional gaming time from the Xbox Store.

Xbox Game Pass Essential, Premium, and Ultimate subscribers will be limited to 5, 10, and 15 hours of cloud gaming per month, respectively. This marks a significant shift from the previous unlimited model. While downloading games remains unlimited, streaming playtime is now metered.

The new policy is expected to impact heavy cloud gamers significantly. For instance, a Game Pass Ultimate subscriber playing 50 hours a month could face substantial extra costs if they need to purchase 35 additional hours. The cost of these extra hours has not yet been disclosed by Microsoft.

Microsoft cites rising infrastructure costs for maintaining its cloud server network as the reason for these changes. The company estimates that only about 4% of its subscribers will be directly affected by the new limits, suggesting that the majority of users do not heavily utilize cloud gaming or stay within the new thresholds.

This move also positions Xbox Cloud Gaming as an 'à la carte' service, potentially attracting users who don't own a console but want to play specific titles. The timing coincides with the highly anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto VI in November, suggesting a strategy to capitalize on a surge of interest from new or lapsed gamers.

This change follows two price increases for Xbox Game Pass over the past two years. While the company did reduce some subscription costs earlier this year, the introduction of playtime limits for cloud gaming suggests a focus on profitability and subscriber retention through a metered usage model.
